qc_blocs.blurb: A small bouldering zone tucked into the L'Agartha hillside in the Dalquier area of Abitibi-Témiscamingue. It holds about fifteen problems, from easy warm-up lines up to a couple of hard testpieces, with many at the easy end and a handful around V3. A low, gentle wall by the entry suits kids or a quick warm-up, a big cracked boulder carries several lines, and further along taller monoliths offer shorter, steeply overhanging problems. A few boulders have anchors on top, so the harder ones with poor landings can be climbed on a rope. Expect a long walk-in on forest trails.
qc_blocs.approach: Reached by the same trail as the L'Agartha crag, about 2.1 km on foot from the main parking lot.

qc_d_la_guignol_e.blurb: A short wall inside the river gorge at St-Alban in the Portneuf region, known as a winter and dry-tooling venue. Fourteen lines here: mostly mixed routes spread from M5 to M9, plus a few bolted lines in the 5.12 range. The walk from the parking area is only a few minutes. The gorge sits a short way below a dam, so water levels can change fast and the river controls how much of the cliff you can reach; this sector stays reachable at higher flows than most of the others. Check river conditions before you go.

qc_2_z_br_e.blurb: A tight, enclosed amphitheatre on Mont King above Val-David in the Laurentians, set between the Toit de Ben roof and the Impériale face, with big slabs at its foot. It is mostly a trad crag with a single sport line, and the climbing is hard: a couple of moderate pitches, but most routes sit in the 5.11 to 5.14 range. The headline line is a steep, sustained finger crack through roofs that is known for seeping and staying wet, so dry weather helps a lot. The hike in from the road runs roughly twenty minutes, mostly uphill.

qc_a_chico_valse.blurb: A beginner-friendly sector on Mont Césaire in Val-David, in the Laurentians. Most of its fourteen climbs are trad, with a couple of top-rope lines and one sport route, and the grades run from easy terrain up through the 5.8 range, with one route at 5.10. The left end has an angled wall with many options and glue-in anchors for setting up top ropes, which makes it a good place to learn; the right end holds the harder lines. A trail on the left leads to the top of the cliff.

qc_mur_principal.blurb: One of the four sectors of Paroi Écho in the Poisson Blanc regional park, Laurentides, reached by boat rather than on foot. Fourteen routes, mostly bolted with a few trad and top-rope lines, ranging from about 5.8 to 5.12-, with 5.10 the most common grade. It is the wall where you can belay from a canoe, so the water level changes the feel of the starts: when the lake is low the bottom section is harder and the first bolt is high, and a stickclip is worth carrying. The wall gets sun in the afternoon.

qc_03_bonsai.blurb: Sector 03 of L'Amphitheatre, the quartzite sport cliff near Saint-André-de-Kamouraska in the Bas-Saint-Laurent. Fourteen routes, mostly bolted with a couple of top-rope lines and two trad climbs, mostly easy to moderate up to about 5.8, with a pair of harder lines at 5.11 and 5.12. The cliff as a whole has a fine view from the top, and it can be crowded on weekends.

qc_peace.blurb: The right-hand end of La Grande Falaise at Kékéko in Abitibi-Témiscamingue. A tall face of about 40 m with long, two-pitch lines, half sport and half trad across fourteen routes. Most are 5.10 to 5.11, with a couple of easier 5.9s and one at the 5.12 level. It catches sun from morning into mid-afternoon. The trail from the end of the road is marked with blue flags, and the sector is reached by walking along the cliff base to the peace sign painted on the wall.

qc_c_mur_des_5_10.blurb: A wall at Lac Gervais in the Laurentides that lives up to its name: most of its fourteen routes sit at 5.10, with a few at 5.9 and a pair at 5.11. Mostly bolted, with four traditional lines, including mixed routes that need natural gear. A stickclip helps on some of the sport lines. The base is found by taking the side path off the main trail and walking a short way to a pair of dead trees.
